headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and associated infrastructure, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer and environmental advocates, Governor's administration, Dominion Energy (with caveats).
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Large Users
news_summary: Virginia HB 1393 directs the primary electric provider to establish rates for large energy users (25 MW or more) to recover costs for increasing electric generating capacity, effectively requiring data centers to pay for their own infrastructure. This legislation aims to prevent these costs from being passed on to residential customers, potentially lowering their bills.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing state regulators with better data for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, environmental groups, policymakers, water resource planners.
opponents: Data center industry (concerned about reporting requirements).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Data Center Water Use Tracking
news_summary: Virginia's General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report water volumes provided to data centers, including potable and reclaimed water. This legislation aims to address concerns about the lack of centralized tracking of data center water use, providing crucial data for state and local water resource planning, especially given the industry's significant water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Community advocates, residents concerned about noise and siting, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Delegate Sam Rasoul.
opponents: Data center developers (concerned about increased regulatory hurdles and costs).
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Noise, Siting Studies
news_summary: HB 153, now law, mandates that developers of large data centers conduct site assessments to examine noise profiles on residential units and schools within 500 feet. It also grants localities the power to require assessments of potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, aiming to address community concerns about data center proliferation.
